reason: E1 supports the role of high configurational entropy in stabilizing solid solutions at high temperatures, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that lattice distortion reduces atomic diffusivity or that this effect suppresses phase segregation. E2 mentions distortion effects in the context of catalytic electronic properties, not diffusion or phase stability. The key mechanistic link between distortion and suppressed diffusion is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid solution phase at high temperatures.
Lattice distortion (from atomic size mismatch) reduces atomic diffusivity.
Reduced diffusivity suppresses phase segregation and chemical ordering.
The combination of entropy stabilization and reduced diffusivity maintains homogeneity up to 1923 K.
Greater lattice distortion leads to better stability than lower distortion at similar entropy.
